description: Steering amendments for the Common Workspace Frame (CR-NR-115). Add an eighth core mechanism to framework-conformance.md, add the content-area-only rule to wiring-standard.md, and add a cross-reference in workspace-conformance.md. ASCII-only. Rules MUST cite the REAL code names created in FEAT-001/FEAT-002. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 (for the implemented names).
steps: Read context.json and the findings of FEAT-001 (note_action_dispatched, format_last_action, render_message_line, workspace_status_segment, message_line, last_action_at) and FEAT-002 (apply_common_frame + its file). Work inside the worktree. ASCII-only per documentation-charset.md.

framework-conformance.md: ADD core mechanism '8. Common Workspace Frame (CR-NR-115)' to the core-framework list: the shell owns the eight frame elements (window title bar, menu bar, full tab bar, centered workspace title, Command ===> line, Message_Line, Status_Bar, pfshow key bar), drawn once around every Workspace; a Workspace owns ONLY its content area + one status-bar segment; DO NOT redraw a frame element inside content; DO NOT draw chrome per-Context. Cite the actual names: the apply_common_frame chrome helper (crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/common_frame.rs), the additive message_line + last_action_at shell state + note_action_dispatched seam, the workspace_status_segment per-Kind status seam. ADD to the 'what counts as a framework change' list: reshaping the common frame or the common-vs-unique boundary, or adding/removing a frame element, needs owner confirmation.

wiring-standard.md: in the 'View Integration' concern AND the 'When adding a NEW workspace' checklist, ADD that a new workspace fills ONLY the content area and contributes ONE status-bar segment (workspace_status_segment); it never draws the title bar / menu bar / tab bar / command line / message line / status bar / PF-key line itself -- the shell common frame (apply_common_frame) provides those.

workspace-conformance.md: ADD a short cross-reference tying the focus contract to the common-frame contract -- both are 'every workspace MUST ...' obligations (the focus contract via WorkspaceContext/InteriorFocus; the common-frame contract via the shell-owned frame + content-area-only ownership).
Verify ASCII-only with the documentation-charset.md pattern over .kiro/steering/*.md and confirm no new non-ASCII (outside the allowed box-drawing range) was introduced. Commit locally; do not push.
acceptance_criteria: framework-conformance.md lists an eighth core mechanism 'Common Workspace Frame (CR-NR-115)' citing apply_common_frame, message_line/last_action_at/note_action_dispatched, and workspace_status_segment by their real names, and its 'what counts as a framework change' list includes reshaping the common frame / boundary / a frame element.
wiring-standard.md states a new workspace fills only the content area + one status-bar segment and never draws any of the seven other frame elements.
workspace-conformance.md cross-references the focus contract to the common-frame contract.
All three files remain ASCII-only (box-drawing allowed only where already permitted).
findings:
DONE on branch common-frame-impl. Docs-only; ASCII-only confirmed (Select-String '[^\x00-\x7F\u2500-\u257F]' over the three files returned empty, rc 0). Sections amended:

1. .kiro/steering/framework-conformance.md:
   - 'The core framework (the load-bearing mechanisms)' list: ADDED mechanism '8. Common Workspace Frame (CR-NR-115)'. States the shell owns the eight frame elements (window title bar, menu bar, FULL tab bar, centered workspace title, Command ===> line, Message_Line, Status_Bar, pfshow PF-key bar) drawn once; a Workspace owns ONLY its content area + one status-bar segment; DO NOT redraw a frame element inside content / draw chrome per-Context. Cites the REAL FEAT-001/FEAT-002 names: live frame in shell/render_status.rs (render_status_bar + render_message_line) and panel order in shell/update.rs (render_key_label_bar -> render_status_bar -> render_message_line); snapshot/capture via WorkbenchShell::apply_common_frame (crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/common_frame.rs) called in shell/screen_provider.rs::active_screen_capture; additive shell state message_line: Vec<String> + last_action_at: Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Local>> (shell/state.rs); per-action seam note_action_dispatched() (shell/actions.rs) invoked at begin_command_line (shell/commands_line.rs) and dispatch_bound_command (shell/target_dispatch.rs); status text from format_last_action() ('Last: HH:MM') + active_profile_label() ('Prof: <name>') with no RUNNING; per-Kind seam workspace_status_segment() (shell/render_status.rs).
   - 'What counts as a framework change (needs express confirmation)' list: ADDED an entry for reshaping the Common Workspace Frame or the common-vs-unique boundary, or adding/removing a frame element, or moving an element between the shell frame and the content area (CR-NR-115, mechanism 8).

2. .kiro/steering/wiring-standard.md:
   - 'View Integration' concern: ADDED a bullet that a new workspace fills ONLY its content area and contributes ONE status-bar segment via workspace_status_segment (shell/render_status.rs), never drawing the title bar / menu bar / tab bar / Command ===> line / Message_Line / Status_Bar / PF-key bar -- the shell common frame (apply_common_frame / render_status.rs / update.rs) provides those (CR-NR-115, framework-conformance mechanism 8).
   - 'Implementation checklist (follow in order)' step 6: ADDED the same content-area-only + workspace_status_segment obligation.
   - 'Anti-patterns (do NOT do these)' list: ADDED redrawing any common-frame element inside a Context instead of filling only the content area and returning a workspace_status_segment.

3. .kiro/steering/workspace-conformance.md:
   - ADDED section 'Relationship to the Common Workspace Frame (CR-NR-115)' (after 'When adding a NEW workspace') cross-referencing the focus contract (WorkspaceContext::render -> InteriorFocus via render_workspace_context / apply_interior_focus) to the common-frame contract (shell-owned eight-element frame + content-area-only ownership + workspace_status_segment), framed as the two complementary 'every workspace MUST ...' obligations.

No source code changed; no verification commands beyond the ASCII scan were applicable (docs-only FEAT).
